name: Wayanad Chooralmala & Meppadi Debris Flows
trigger: Continuous Extreme Rainfall (>370 mm in 24 hours)
source: NASA GLC / Geological Survey of India (GSI)
description: Massive catastrophic twin landslides originating in the Vellarimala hills above Punchirimattom, travelling down the Iruvanjippuzha river channel and devastating Chooralmala and Mundakkai villages.

name: Shirur Ankola Landslide
trigger: Torrential Monsoon Rain on excavated hill slope
source: NASA GLC / National Disaster Response Force (NDRF)
description: Severe hillock collapse along National Highway 66 following intense southwest monsoon showers, sweeping vehicles into the Gangavali river.

name: Irshalwadi Landslide
trigger: Extreme Monsoon Downpour (>499 mm in 3 days)
source: NASA GLC / Maharashtra Disaster Management Authority
description: Massive hillside collapse burying 17 out of 48 tribal hamlet dwellings located on the steep slopes of Irshalgad fort.

name: Shimla Summer Hill Shiv Temple Slide
source: NASA GLC / HP State Disaster Management Authority
description: Devastating morning slide during a cloudburst event destroying the Shiv Bawdi temple at Summer Hill and collapsing railway track.

name: Koottickal & Kokkayar Landslides
trigger: Low Pressure Cloudburst (>250 mm in 12 hours)
source: NASA GLC / Kerala State Disaster Management Authority (KSDMA)
description: Multiple flash floods and steep slope failures in Western Ghats valleys triggered by localized extreme precipitation.

name: Pettimudi Tea Plantation Landslide
trigger: Prolonged Torrential Monsoon (>600 mm in 72 hours)
description: Massive hill collapse near Rajamala at 10 PM burying four lines of tea plantation workers' residential quarters under deep mud and rock debris.

name: Kavalappara & Puthumala Landslides
trigger: Extreme Monsoon Rainfall (>400 mm in 48 hours)
description: Two massive separate hillside collapses triggered simultaneously on saturated Western Ghats hillocks, engulfing residential colonies.

name: Malin Village Landslide
trigger: Heavy Monsoon Downpour (>108 mm in 24 hrs on saturated slope)
description: Slope failure swept down early morning burying the entire hillside village of Malin while inhabitants were asleep.

name: Kedarnath Glacier & Moraine Outburst Landslide
hazard_type: Debris Flow / Glacial Lake Outburst / Landslide
trigger: Extreme Cloudburst, 375% above normal June rainfall & snowmelt
source: NASA GLC / Wadia Institute of Himalayan Geology
description: Chorabari moraine dam collapse and mountain slope debris cascades funneled directly into the temple township of Kedarnath.

name: Chamoli / Rishiganga Rock & Ice Avalanche
trigger: Rona/Ronti peak hanging glacier rock wedge failure
source: NASA GLC / DRDO DGRE / Science Journal
description: A wedge of rock and glacier ice detached from Ronti peak, falling 1,800 m and mobilizing into a massive slurry downstream into Tapovan.

name: SR 530 / Oso Landslide
description: Deadliest landslide in United States history; unstable glacial deposits on Whitman Bench collapsed across the North Fork Stillaguamish River.

name: Montecito Debris Flows
trigger: Intense Rain (0.54 inches in 5 minutes) on Thomas Fire burn scar
description: Steep denuded chaparral watersheds unleashed boulder-laden mudflows reaching highway 101 within 20 minutes.

name: Jure / Sunkoshi Landslide & Dam Outburst
description: Massive slope detachment dammed the Sunkoshi river, creating a 3 km long lake and severing the Araniko Highway to China.

name: Mocoa Debris Flow
trigger: 130 mm of rain in hours (a third of monthly normal)
description: Three rivers overflowed sending surges of mud, rocks and trees ripping through 17 neighborhoods of Mocoa.

name: Casamicciola Terme Ischia Landslide
description: Detachment from Mount Epomeo swept vehicles and residences down into the port of Casamicciola.

name: Enga Landslide
trigger: Torrential Rainfall following tectonic seismic destabilization
source: NASA GLC / UN PNG Disaster Assessment
description: Mount Mungalo collapsed at 3 AM completely burying Yambali village under 6 to 8 meters of rubble.
